releases.body:
**opencode V1 support.** The package now ships only the opencode 2.x entry (`{ id, setup }`); the classic `server` factory, the `deprecation` option and its notice log are gone. opencode 2.x is required.

- **Streaming stats, TUI module and self-update.** The plugin no longer measures TTFT/TPS, renders a stats line or `/stats`, writes handoff files, auto-registers a TUI entry, or probes npm for updates — opencode 2.x owns stats, and `opencode plugin update` owns package updates. The `stats`, `statsDebug` and `tui` options are gone with them.
- **Dependencies** `jsonc-parser`, `@opencode-ai/plugin`, `@opencode-ai/sdk` and `@opentui/solid`.
- The plugin now has one responsibility: load the catalog and replace the provider's model list through `ctx.provider.transform` → `draft.models.set`, with the official rate in each record. The catalog loader (mirrors, cache, envelope gate, per-entry gate, all-or-nothing cost adoption) is unchanged.
- `loadCatalog` returns the normalized models directly; the unused `Catalog` wrapper (`generatedAt`/`modelsHash`) is gone.
- `CatalogModel` only keeps the fields the opencode 2.x record consumes. `family`, `quantization` and the raw `input` list no longer survive normalization.
- `README.md` / `README.es.md` are opencode 2.x only: install, how it works, the three remaining options and pricing. The V1 instructions, support matrix, stats/TUI/self-update sections and their screenshots are gone.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/srnoob2570/opencode-ollama-cloud/compare/v0.1.13...v0.2.0

The TUI module loads under opencode V2. The package advertises a TUI entry through `exports["./tui"]`, and 2.x resolves it from `node_modules`, where the host does not apply the Solid JSX transform. The raw JSX in `plugin/tui.tsx` therefore fell back to React's runtime and the plugin failed with `Cannot find package 'react'`. The TUI entry now ships precompiled as `plugin/tui.js`, with JSX compiled to the `@opentui/solid/jsx-runtime` specifier that the host rewrites, and the module exports the V2 contract `{ id, setup }` next to the V1 `tui` factory. Verified end to end on opencode 2.0.15: the setup registers the stats line slot, the update badge and the `/stats` command, with no react error.

- New catalog models appear again. A single malformed entry in the published artifact (`clef:27b`, a decision model that publishes no output limit) rejected the whole document, so the loader silently fell back to the stale disk cache and every model published after 2026-10-15 — `beam` among them — stayed invisible. The loader now validates the document's envelope and gates each entry on its own: a broken entry is dropped with a warning while every usable model still loads.

- `setup(ctx)` for the V2 TUI host. It renders the live stats line in the `session_prompt_right` slot, registers a `/stats` command in the command palette and shows the update badge. The command layer is registered from inside an `app` slot render, because `ctx.keymap.layer` needs the host's Keymap provider, which exists only in the rendered tree.

- `package.json` `exports["./tui"]` points at the precompiled `plugin/tui.js`, which `files` ships. `bun run build:tui` compiles `plugin/tui.tsx` with Bun's automatic JSX runtime (`jsxImportSource: "@opentui/solid"`). A pre-commit hook rebuilds the file when the source changes, and `.prettierignore` keeps the generated file out of formatting.
- Decision models are excluded from the catalog. An entry marked `x_ollama.decision: true` serves Ollama's `/v1/systemone`, not `/api/chat`; opencode cannot use it, so the loader skips it by marker. A partial or malformed `cost` block adopts nothing: the model serves rateless ($0) instead of a wrong price, and `output`/`cache_read` rates of $0 are adopted as legitimate free rates.

- The READMEs and `docs/research/soporte-v1-v2.md` no longer claim that V2 cannot load third-party TUI plugins. V2 loads them through the plugin registry: the package exposes `exports["./tui"]` and the module exports `{ id, setup }`.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/srnoob2570/opencode-ollama-cloud/compare/v0.1.12...v0.1.13

- Support for **opencode V2** (2.x). The entry module now exports the dual shape `{id, setup, server}`: opencode 1.x reads `.server` (the classic factory, unchanged) and opencode 2.x validates `id + setup` and runs `setup(ctx)` against the v2 plugin context. Under V2 the plugin injects the catalog with official pricing through `ctx.provider.transform` → `draft.models.set` (verified end-to-end against opencode 2.0.15: the 20 catalog models appear and generation works). The transform is only registered after the catalog loads — on failure, models.dev's `ollama-cloud` fallback stays alive. Full findings in `docs/research/soporte-v1-v2.md`.

The TUI plugin no longer registers its own /model command. It shadowed opencode's native /model picker, which now opens as expected. The model card goes with it: family, quantization, capabilities, limits, release date, official rates and token sizes. The stats line, /stats and the pricing the plugin reports are unchanged.

### Changed

- The catalog is no longer built in this repo. The plugin consumes a single `catalog.json` from [srnoob2570/ollama-cloud-catalog](https://github.com/srnoob2570/ollama-cloud-catalog), where GitHub Actions build it behind a hash gate: a change in Ollama's `/v1/models` list triggers a full re-extraction, specs come from `/api/show` and a model parses the rate card. A failed scrape aborts upstream instead of publishing a degraded catalog. The local `scripts/`, the schemas and the pricing workflows are gone.
- Pricing ships embedded in each model's `cost` block instead of a separate `catalog/pricing.json`. The plugin keeps showing the standard off-peak rate; peak windows live in the artifact's `x_ollama` extension. The cost counter behaves the same as before.
- The model card always labels quantization as "(declared)". The value comes from Ollama's `/api/show` through the upstream pipeline, so the old "(implicit)" source distinction no longer exists.
- `catalogUrl` no longer means "catalog without rates". A custom URL is tried first; when it fails or serves an invalid document, the official mirrors stay as fallback.
- Documentation: the READMEs claimed the stats line renders "next to the token counter". It does not, and never did: the line renders on the right side of the prompt row (the row with the model name), one row above opencode's own context/cost counter, which is a separate sidebar line the plugin does not touch. The example line now shows only what the plugin renders (`38.2 tok/s · TTFT 380 ms · Session average`).

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/srnoob2570/opencode-ollama-cloud/compare/v0.1.9...v0.1.10
